title: Throughput collapse for mixed-variant requests causing tokens/sec and TTFT spike
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted API tier + two Dedicated accounts + one Private cluster) reported a sudden degradation in tokens/sec and first-token time (TTFT) for multi-model/multi-variant requests. Impact measured as ~60% drop in tokens/sec and median TTFT increase from ~180ms to ~680ms on affected worker pools. This started after a staged rollout of an optimization that added a weighted kernel-selection heuristic and a faster variant-probing path for quantized variants.

Initial triage: we observed correlated spikes in: kernel-switching counts, KV-prefetch requests, worker reassignment events, and multiplex queue length. Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by trace replays): the new kernel-selection weights caused the scheduler to prefer short-warm kernels for part of the fanout; simultaneously, the variant-probing path triggered parallel prefetches for quantized variants across shards. The combination produced a burst of KV prefetch work and kernel warmups that saturated GPU worker threads and starved the multiplexing pipeline, leading to large TTFTs and lower sustained tokens/sec.

Why this is customer-facing: Dedicated and Private clusters with mixed-model workloads (e.g., long context + short chat queries to different model variants) saw interleaved requests that amplified the prefetched warmups. Hosted customers on high-concurrency routes also experienced knock-on effects when shared pools briefly saturated.

Immediate action plan (hotfix timeline):
1) Emergency rollback (short term) — revert scheduler weight change and disable aggressive variant-probing path for the next 6 hours. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289) — target: 03-10 23:00 UTC.
2) Throttle variant probing — add a per-model probe rate limiter and exponential backoff for failed probes. Patch branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/throttle-variant-probe.
3) KV prefetch rate-limiter — implement adaptive token-budgeted prefetching (soft cap) to avoid burst storms. Prototype implemented in branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/kv-prefetch-rate-limit.
4) Canary rollout — Hosted (canary pool) for 2 hrs, then Dedicated small customers, then Private clusters via ops schedule. Rollback plan: automatic revert if TTFT increases >30% vs baseline or tokens/sec drops >20% on canary monitors.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- tokens/sec recovers to within 10% of baseline on canary within 45 minutes of rollout.
- median TTFT back to <= 220ms on affected pools.
- no error-rate increase or OOM events on canary workers.
- clear customer confirmation messages for the three impacted accounts.

Notes for follow-up permanents:
- Revisit kernel-selection heuristic with worker-affinity constraints to avoid warmup storms.
- Add telemetry to track per-variant probe concurrency and KV-prefetch queue depth.
- Add a regression test that simulates heterogeneous fanout (mixing long-context + short-chat + quantized variants) to detect similar regressions during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Canary tokens/sec within 10% of baseline within 45m
No increase in worker OOMs or retry loops
